answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a separate bond before bidding, with withdrawals delayed for 30 days. A steady pulse of new accounts therefore demands fresh capital: copying a profile can mirror its appearance, but cannot reuse a bond already pledged to another identity. The market can still harbor fake agents, yet an attacker running 1,000 of them must immobilize 1,000 bonds and bear the financing cost throughout the delay.
